setlist.title: Beat it on Down the Line

liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Shakedown St** (1 review): The opening Shakedown felt like Jerry's reassurance that he'd be back, to the reviewer [15]
- **Beat it on Down the Line** (1 review): Reviewer calls this the most killer version of the song they have heard [11]
- **I need A Miracle** (1 review): Reviewer finds this track unlistenable because the recording totally breaks down [22]
- **Scarlet Begonias** (1 review): Reviewer hoped for a Scarlet-Fire all the way to New Haven and got one [14]
- **Not Fade Away** (1 review): A fine transition jam out of Drums leads into a long, jammed-out, somewhat spacey version [16]
- **Black Peter** (1 review): Reviewer says this is the longest Black Peter ever, and probably the slowest [16]

## Setlist highlights

- **Bobby Welcomes Jerry back**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [23]
- **Heart Of Me**: mythic rare: 2 archived performances [23]
- **unruliness**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [23]

## The recordings

- **gd1979-01-17.mtx.mccabe.91783.sbeok.flac16** (recommended): matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 23 songs; 199 min; rated 2.5/5 by 4 [1]. Said about its sound: Matrix sounds decent through From the Heart of Me, then breaks down into digital dropouts [22]
- **gd79-01-17.rolfe.pujol-vernon.12200.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 22 songs; 193 min; rated 3.88/5 by 8 [2]. Said about its sound: Reviewer found the audience recording's sound and musical quality poor; Reviewer calls the audience recording's sound excellent, so good that soundboards would be unnecessary; The SHN files for Scarlet and Fire cut out at about four and six minutes respectively [2][12][16][17]
- **gd1979-01-17.nak301.rolfe.miller.99009.sbeok.flac16**: source not stated; 22 songs; 191 min; rated 4.56/5 by 9 [3]. Said about its sound: Rich, full sound, not tinny or distant, and the band's energy comes through fully [20]
- **gd1979-01-17.sbd.mhg.77208.flac16**: soundboard; 22 songs; 178 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [5]. Said about its sound: Uploader doesn't know what EQ was applied to the master cassette source [5]
- **gd1979-01-17.nak300.glassberg.85101.flac24**: audience recording; 21 songs; 196 min; rated 4.67/5 by 3 [7]. Said about its sound: Reviewer praises the audience recording's sound quality, crediting Barry G [19]

## Around the show

- A rescheduled November 1978 show; the band seemed to compensate with an especially long set [11]
- Jerry played with fierce intensity throughout the first set, according to the reviewer [11]
- Jerry's illness cancelled the November 1978 date; the makeup show fell on the reviewer's 18th birthday [14]
- Lights went down and Bobby and Mickey told the crowd Jerry was on a respirator; no one booed [15]
- Reviewer was on the floor; notes the New Haven Coliseum has since been demolished [18]
- Perrotti turned 18 at this show; he had also made the trip on 11.25.78 when Jerry fell ill [1]
- Show was rescheduled from November 25, 1978 [3]
- Perrotti turned 18 at this show; he had also made the trip on 11.25.78 when Jerry fell ill [5]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1979-01-17.mtx.mccabe.91783.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Matrix created in Adobe Audition 3.0. Plugins included Nomad Factory and Izotope. Matrix is set at 50/50 blend.; transferred by D. McCabe; source: SBD: new transfer 2008 via Lunatec V2 preamp > Korg MR-1000; AUD Source: gd1979-01-17.fob.glassberg.motb.0023.85101.flac24 [1]. Also: Soundboard came from Vince Perrotti via Peter Hedeman; a friend patched in and gave him the boards the next day [1]
- **gd79-01-17.rolfe.pujol-vernon.12200.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Steve Rolfe; transferred by Marc Pujol; source: Audience Recording: TEAC PC-10 with nak 700 mic's pole-mounted fob [2]. Also: Reviewer holds third-generation soundboard copies with a few glitches, obtained as a gift about two weeks later; DAT to WAV transfer by Marc Pujol, from a DAT clone via Dave Minor [2][14]
- **gd1979-01-17.nak301.rolfe.miller.99009.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Steve Rolfe; transferred by Charlie Miller; source: (FOB) Nakamichi 300/CP1 -> Cassette Master (Sony TC-158/Maxell UDXL-I90/Dolby B) [3]. Also: Described as a front-of-board audience recording, by Rolfe and Miller; Gaps filled from another source; pitch correction done with help from Joe B. Jones [3][20]
- **gd1979-01-17.sbd.mhg.77208.flac16**: source: SBD: MC > EQ > CDR > EAC > SHN > patched w/ SHN ID # 12200 > FLAC [5]. Also: Soundboard came from Vince Perrotti via Peter Hedeman; a friend patched in and gave him the boards [5]
- **gd1979-01-17.nak300.glassberg.85101.flac24**: taped by Barry Glassberg; transferred by A. Egert; source: Audience FOB Recording, Sec 9f Seat 4 Orchestra - 9ft pole Media: Maxell UDXL II 90 Lineage: Nakamichi CM300's > Sony 158SD > MAC [7]
